source_text: τοῖς ἄλλοις ἅπασιν ἁγιασμοῦ χορηγὸς καὶ συνδοτὴρ, ὡς Θεὸς, τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρὶ, μεθ' ἡμῶν ἁγιάζεται κατὰ τὸ ἀνθρώπινον· καὶ τοῦτό ἐστιν ἡ λεγομένη κένωσις. Ὁ γὰρ ἅγιος κατὰ φύσιν ὡς Θεὸς, δεδεῆσθαι λέγεται τοῦ ἁγιάζοντος Θεοῦ· καὶ τοῦτό φησιν ὁ μακάριος Πέτρος· «Ἵνα τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ, ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ Θεὸς Πνεύματι ἁγίῳ.» Οὐκοῦν περὶ τὸ ἀνθρώπινον ἡ χρίσις, καὶ τῆς σαρκὸς ὁ ἁγιασμὸς, τῆς οὐ κατὰ φύσιν ἁγίας, ἀλλ' ὡς ἐν μεθέξει τῇ παρὰ Θεοῦ· θύραθεν γὰρ τοῖς κτίσμασιν ὁ ἁγιασμὸς, καὶ εἰσποιητῶς παρὰ Θεοῦ καταπλουτοῦσι τὴν χάριν. Χρίεται δὲ τοῖς ἄλλοις ὁμοῦ, καὶ τῆς κατὰ νόμον λατρείας τὸ θυσιαστήριον. Ἅγιος γὰρ καὶ ὁ νόμος, καλῶν εἰς ἐπίγνωσιν τοῦ κατὰ φύσιν Θεοῦ, καὶ δικαιοσύνης εἴδησιν τοῖς ἀκροωμένοις ἐντιθεὶς, καὶ εἰς ἀρχὰς ἀγαθότητος ἀποφέρων τοὺς παιδευομένους· «Ἀρχὴ γὰρ, φησὶν, ὁδοῦ ἀγαθῆς τὸ ποιεῖν τὰ δίκαια.» Γράφει δέ που καὶ ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, «Ὥστε ὁ μὲν νόμος ἅγιος, καὶ ἡ ἐντολὴ ἁγία, καὶ δικαία καὶ ἀγαθή.» Ἅγιος δὲ ἁγίων ὁ νόμος, οὐ κατά γε τὴν σκιὰν, ἀλλ' ὅτι πρὸς θεωρίαν εἰ μετατρέποιτο τὴν πνευματικὴν, αὐτὸν ἡμῖν οἱ τύποι διακεκράγασι τὸν Χριστὸν, τὸν Ἅγιον ἁγίων ἀληθῶς· ἁγιάζει γὰρ ὡς Θεὸς τῷ ἰδίῳ καταχρίων πνεύματι τοὺς ἐν μεθέξει γεγονότας αὐτοῦ διὰ τῆς πίστεως. Ἐγηγερμένης δὲ δὴ, καὶ μὴν καὶ ἐλαίῳ τῷ ἁγίῳ κατακεχρισμένης τῆς ἁγίας σκηνῆς, τὸ μετὰ τοῦτο λέγωμεν, εἰ δοκεῖ. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Πάνυ μὲν οὖν. {ΚΥΡ.} Γέγραπται τοίνυν ὡδί· «Καὶ συνετέλεσε Μωσῆς πάντα τὰ ἔργα, καὶ συνεκάλυψεν ἡ νεφέλη τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ δόξης Κυρίου ἐπληρώθη ἡ σκηνή. Καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθη Μωσῆς εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ μαρτυρίου, ὅτι ἐπεσκίαζεν ἐπ' αὐτὴν ἡ νεφέλη, καὶ δόξης Κυρίου ἐπλήσθη ἡ σκηνή. Ἡνίκα δὲ ἀνέβη ἀπὸ τῆς σκηνῆς, ἀνεζεύγνυσαν οἱ υἱοὶ Ἰσραὴλ σὺν τῇ ἀπαρτίᾳ αὐτῶν· εἰ δὲ μὴ ἀνέβη ἡ νεφέλη, οὐκ ἀνεζεύγνυσαν ἕως τῆς ἡμέρας, ἧς ἀνέβη ἡ νεφέλη· νεφέλη γὰρ ἦν ἐπὶ τῆς σκηνῆς ἡμέρας, καὶ πῦρ ἦν ἐπ' αὐτῆς νυκτὸς, ἐναντίον παντὸς Ἰσραὴλ, ἐν πάσαις ταῖς ἀναζυγαῖς αὐτῶν.» Ἀναδεδειγμένης γὰρ ἐν κόσμῳ τῆς ἁγίας καὶ ἀληθεστέρας σκηνῆς, τοῦτ' ἔστι, τῆς ἐξ ἐθνῶν Ἐκκλησίας, φῶς περιελάμπετο Χριστοῦ, καὶ ἡ νεφέλη ὥσπερ τις πνευματικὴ δρόσος ἡμᾶς τοῖς ἄνωθεν πλουσίως καταπιαίνουσα, τὸν θεῖον ναὸν ἀναπίμπλησι. Πλὴν, οὐκ ἠδυνήθη, φησὶν, εἰσελθεῖν ὁ Μωσῆς, οὐ γὰρ εἰσβέβηκεν ὁ Ἰσραὴλ, τὴν τοῦ θείου φωτὸς προσβολὴν ἐνεγκεῖν οὐ δυνάμενος, ἐπείτοι οὐδὲ συνῆκε τὸ Χριστοῦ μυστήριον, ἀλλ' οὐδὲ προσήκατο τὸν ἐν πνεύματι φωτισμὸν, οὐδὲ τεθέαται τοῖς τῆς διανοίας ὄμμασι τὴν δόξαν Κυρίου, ᾧ καὶ ὡς ἐν τύπῳ νεφέλης, ἀπαίροντι μὲν τοῦ κόσμου καὶ πρὸς τὰ ἄνω βαδίζοντι, συναπαίρομεν κατ' ἴχνος ἰόντες τὸ δεσποτικὸν ἐνεκαίνισε γὰρ ἡμῖν τὴν πρόσφατόν τε καὶ ζῶσαν ὁδὸν, τὴν εἰς τὰ ἄνω φημὶ καὶ ἐν οὐρανῷ, ἀναπαυομένῳ δὲ ὥσπερ
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing: he himself being the] provider (χορηγός) and co-giver (συνδοτήρ) of sanctification (ἁγιασμός) to all others, as God, with the God and Father, is sanctified with us according to the human (κατὰ τὸ ἀνθρώπινον); and this is the so-called emptying (κένωσις). For the one holy by nature (κατὰ φύσιν) as God is said to have needed (δέομαι) the sanctifying God; and blessed Peter says this: '[Jesus] the one from Nazareth, how God anointed (χρίω) him with Holy Spirit'. So the anointing (χρίσις) is about the human, and the sanctification is of the flesh (σάρξ), not holy by nature but as in participation (μέθεξις) from God; for sanctification is from outside (θύραθεν) to creatures (κτίσματα), and by adoption/acquisition (εἰσποιητῶς) from God they are enriched (καταπλουτέω) with grace (χάρις). Anointed with the others is also the altar of the worship (λατρεία) according to law. For the law too is holy, calling to knowledge (ἐπίγνωσις) of the God by nature, placing knowledge (εἴδησις) of righteousness in the hearers, and carrying the instructed (παιδεύω) to beginnings of goodness (ἀγαθότης): 'For the beginning of a good way is to do the just things'. Divine Paul writes: 'So the law is holy, and the commandment holy and just and good'. The law is Holy of holies, not according to the shadow (σκιά), but because, if turned to spiritual contemplation (θεωρία πνευματική), the types have cried aloud (διακράζω) to us Christ himself, the truly Holy of holies (masc.); for as God he sanctifies, anointing with his own Spirit those who have come into participation of him through faith. The holy tent being raised (ἐγείρω) and anointed with holy oil, let us say what follows, if it seems good. PALL. Certainly. CYR. It is written thus: 'And Moses completed (συντελέω) all the works, and the cloud (νεφέλη) covered the tent of witness (μαρτύριον), and the tent was filled with glory of the Lord. And Moses could not enter the tent of witness, because the cloud overshadowed (ἐπισκιάζω) it, and the tent was filled with glory of the Lord. When [it] went up from the tent, the sons of Israel broke camp (ἀναζεύγνυμι) with their baggage (ἀπαρτία); if the cloud did not go up, they did not break camp until the day on which the cloud went up; for cloud was on the tent by day and fire on it by night before all Israel in all their departures (ἀναζυγαί)'. For the holy and truer tent being shown (ἀναδείκνυμι) in the world, i.e. the Church from nations, light of Christ shone around (περιλάμπω), and the cloud, as a spiritual dew (δρόσος) richly fattening (καταπιαίνω) us with the things from above, fills the divine temple (ναός). But Moses could not enter, for Israel did not enter, unable to bear the assault (προσβολή) of divine light, since it neither understood the mystery (μυστήριον) of Christ, nor accepted the illumination (φωτισμός) in spirit, nor beheld with the eyes of the understanding (διάνοια) the glory of the Lord, with whom also, as in type of cloud, departing (ἀπαίρω) from the world and walking to the things above, we depart together, going in the Master's (δεσποτικόν) track (ἴχνος); for he inaugurated (ἐγκαινίζω) for us the fresh (πρόσφατος) and living way, I mean to the things above and in heaven; and resting (ἀναπαύομαι) as it were...
pass_b_english: Cyril: …as God, together with God the Father, supplies and bestows sanctification on all others, is himself sanctified with us in his humanity; and this is what is called the self-emptying (Philippians 2:7). For he who is holy by nature, as God, is said to have needed God to sanctify him. Blessed Peter says this too: ‘Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit’ (Acts 10:38). So the anointing concerns his humanity, and the sanctification belongs to the flesh, which is not holy by nature but holy by participation in what comes from God. For sanctification comes to created things from outside, and they are enriched with grace as something added to them by God. Together with the rest, the altar of the worship under the law is anointed too. For the law also is holy: it calls its hearers to the knowledge of him who is God by nature, plants in them an understanding of righteousness, and carries those it instructs on to the beginnings of goodness. ‘For the beginning of a good way,’ it says, ‘is to do what is right’ (Proverbs 16:7, Septuagint). And the inspired Paul writes somewhere: ‘So the law is holy, and the commandment is holy and righteous and good’ (Romans 7:12). The law is holy of holies, not in its shadow, but because, if it is turned to spiritual contemplation, its types proclaim aloud to us Christ himself, who is truly the Holy of Holies. For as God he sanctifies those who have come to share in him through faith, anointing them with his own Spirit. Now that the holy tent has been set up, and anointed with the holy oil as well, let us speak of what comes next, if you agree.

Cyril: This, then, is what is written: ‘And Moses finished all the works. And the cloud covered the tent of witness, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord. And Moses was not able to enter the tent of witness, because the cloud overshadowed it, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord. Whenever it went up from the tent, the sons of Israel set out with their baggage; but if the cloud did not go up, they did not set out until the day on which the cloud went up. For the cloud was on the tent by day, and fire was on it by night, before all Israel in all their journeys’ (Exodus 40:33–38). For when the holy and truer tent, that is, the Church from the Gentiles, had been revealed in the world, the light of Christ shone around it, and the cloud, like a kind of spiritual dew richly nourishing us with what comes from above, fills the divine temple. Yet Moses, it says, was not able to enter; for Israel did not go in, since it could not bear the force of the divine light. For it neither understood the mystery of Christ, nor accepted the enlightening that comes in the Spirit, nor beheld the glory of the Lord with the eyes of the mind. And with him, as in the type of the cloud, when he departs from the world and goes on to the things above, we depart too, following in the Master’s footsteps; for he opened for us the new and living way (Hebrews 10:20), I mean the way to the things above and in heaven. And when he rests, as it were…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril, De adoratione Book 10. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withheld earlier English was not used.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, completing 'the very one who' from section 21. 'Self-emptying' (κένωσις) cited to Philippians 2:7 (ἐκένωσεν). Acts 10:38: PG prints Ἵνα, which cannot stand; the verse reads Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ, so 'Jesus' is read (probably a misread abbreviation of the name); flagged for the source editor. εἰσποιητῶς ('by way of addition/adoption') rendered 'as a gift brought in'. Proverbs 16:7 is the LXX verse (Brenton 16:7, 'The beginning of a good way is to do justly'); it has no counterpart at 16:7 in English Bibles, which follow the Hebrew; the editor may prefer '(Proverbs 16:7, Septuagint)' in the reading text. Holy of holies: neuter for the altar (section 21), masculine for the law (agreeing with νόμος) and for Christ (τὸν Ἅγιον ἁγίων), capitalised only for Christ. Exodus 40:33-38 cited by English numbering (Moses finishing the work is 40:33b; LXX verse division in this chapter differs slightly). The PG text of the quotation lacks 'the cloud' as subject of 'whenever it went up' (LXX has ἡ νεφέλη); translated 'it' as printed. σκηνὴ τοῦ μαρτυρίου rendered 'tent of witness'. 'Eyes of the mind' may echo Ephesians 1:18 and 'beheld the glory of the Lord' 2 Corinthians 3:18; 'following in the Master's footsteps' may echo 1 Peter 2:21; all left uncited as doubtful. Hebrews 10:20: ἐνεκαίνισεν ... ὁδὸν πρόσφατον καὶ ζῶσαν, cited. The section ends mid-sentence ('ἀναπαυομένῳ δὲ ὥσπερ | καὶ καταλύοντι...'), continued in section 23.

changes: μέθεξις kept as the doctrinal term 'participation' (was 'sharing')
εἰσποιητῶς clause recast: 'enriched with grace as something added to them by God'
Proverbs quotation is LXX-only (Brenton 16:7; English 16:7 is a different verse): inline citation now '(Proverbs 16:7, Septuagint)' so readers are not sent to the wrong verse
'the gifts from above' -> 'what comes from above' (τοῖς ἄνωθεν; no added noun)
Fixed a doubled verb: συναπαίρομεν was rendered twice ('we too set out ... we depart with him'); now once
'leads on high and into heaven' -> 'to the things above and in heaven'
Citations checked: Phil 2:7, Acts 10:38 (PG Ἵνα read as 'Jesus', see note), Rom 7:12, Exod 40:33-38 (English numbering), Heb 10:20: correct
